MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
February 19, 2013

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Tuesday,
February 19, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present
were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community
Services Director McPherron, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation
Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada and the City Council presented certificates of appointment to James Villela
(Public Safety and Traffic Commission) and Gia Stokes (Public Safety and Traffic
Commission).

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the presentation of the Independently
Audited Financial Statements for FY 2011-2012, had been moved to the next City Council
meeting given that the auditor/presenter was not able to attend tonight’s meeting.

City Manager Rock informed Council that some temporary taste and odor issues have been
reported, but that these issues were associated with the imported water from the
Metropolitan Water District, and came about from increased methylisoborneol levels, as well
as the shutdown and startup of the Weymouth Plant. City Manager Rock clarified that the
taste and odor issues were from Metropolitan water, not blended water, as the City has not
yet begun distribution of the blended water.

  Page 1 of 1
 5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda item to discuss amending the Lomita
Municipal Code, specifically Section 11-1.70.16, regarding the review and appeals of
Planning Commission decisions. Councilmember Sanchez suggested extending the appeals
process from 15 days to 30 days. Councilmembers Gazeley seconded the motion, which
carried unanimously.

Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda item to discuss reconsideration of
amending the Assembly Uses Ordinance regarding the regulations for setbacks.
Councilmember Traina seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Gazeley
NOES: Mayor Estrada

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Laura Walters, Community Services Representative for the Los Angeles County Fire
Department, reported that in the last month the Los Angeles County Fire Department
responded to some significant residential home fires caused by the fireplaces. Ms. Walters
provided those in attendance with safety tips for fireplace and chimney maintenance.

Dan Cardella, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, informed those in
attendance that the Chamber's next Business Mixer is scheduled to take place on Thursday,
February 28, 2013, at the Lomita Magnet School, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez requested that Items 7.C, 7.E, and 7.H be pulled from the consent
agenda for discussion.

Regarding Item 7.C, Councilmember Sanchez requested clarification on whether the
payment for voucher #509927, for FS Construction, was for sidewalk improvements and
ramps; Councilmember Sanchez received clarification from staff.

In regards to Item 7.E, Councilmember Sanchez inquired as to whether Task #7, which was
listed as an optional task in Attachment A of the Professional Services Agreement with KEC
Engineers, Inc., was part of the Request for Proposal (RFP). In response, Director Damasse
stated that “construction inspection and construction management” were not included in the
overall cost of the agreement with KEC Engineers, Inc., and that another RFP will be issued
for that particular task. Councilmember Traina asked if staff had looked into the possibility of
replacing existing telephone poles with other alternative poles on Eshelman Avenue, to
which Director Damasse responded that alternative telephone poles were not part of the
design, but could be included.

As for Item 7.H, Councilmember Sanchez expressed his concern over potential water
shortages, and questioned whether leasing the City's 637 acre-feet of groundwater rights
  Page 2 of 2
 would be a wise decision. Councilmember Sanchez further added that the City might want
to think about reserving more water rights. Director Damasse responded by stating that 637
acre-feet was a very conservative estimate of the amount of groundwater rights that could
be leased, however, Director Damasse did add that staff would not know for some time how
much water would be needed. Councilmember Savidan suggested holding off on leasing
groundwater rights for the time being.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Traina
seconded the motion, with an addition to Item 7.E, that the design include alternative
telephone poles for the Eshelman Avenue project. The motion carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on
  February 4, 2013, and the Regular City Council Meeting held on February 4, 2013.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Adoption of the Engineering and Traffic (E&T) Survey for Narbonne Avenue regarding
  Speed Limit Postings. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  e. Approval of a Professional Services Agreement with KEC Engineers, Inc., for the
  Eshelman Avenue Street Improvement and Water Main Replacement Project.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  f. Receive and File the Fiscal Year 2011-12 Comprehensive Financial Report (Audit
  Report). RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Approval of Tree City USA Application for Recertification.  RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  h. Report submitting authorization to staff to advertise the City’s anticipated unused
  groundwater rights of up to a maximum of 637 acre-feet for lease to other agencies.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

8. WATER TREATMENT PLANT OPERATOR (NEW CLASSIFICATION)

Assistant City Manager Sugano informed City Council that as the Cypress Water Production
Facility (CWPF) becomes fully operational, the City will need to gradually reduce its reliance
on Waterworks to manage CWPF, and in turn hire its own staff to oversee operations. Given
the coming changes, Assistant City Manager Sugano recommended that the City hire a
licensed Water Treatment Plant Operator, as well as amend Section IV of the Authorized
Positions and Salary Schedule of the adopted FY 2012-2013 Budget, and approve a Letter
of Understanding with the Field Services Unit of the Lomita City Employee's Association
regarding the new classification of the Water Treatment Plant Operator. According to
Assistant City Manager Sugano, by hiring a full-time Water Treatment Plant Operator, the
City would see significant savings through the gradual reduction of reliance on WaterWorks.

  Page 3 of 3
   Councilmember Traina agreed that hiring a full-time Water Treatment Plant Operator is in the
  best interest of ratepayers, but questioned whether the timing was right to hire that particular
  position. Director Damasse responded that it would be prudent to hire a Water Treatment
  Plant Operator from the very start of CWPF operations in order for the new Water Treatment
  Plant Operator to receive proper training from WaterWorks. Director Damasse further added
  that the transition period, from WaterWorks to full City operations of CWPF, is estimated to
  take between six and eight months, which in turn would be a sufficient period of time for the
  new Water Treatment Plant Operator to receive comprehensive training.

  In response to Councilmember’s Traina question as to whether one Water Treatment Plant
  Operator would be sufficient to run CWPF, Director Damasse stated that in the future staff
  plans on having a back-up to the Water Treatment Plant Operator. Director Damasse further
  added that some existing staff members have already obtained proper treatment operator
  licenses, and that a licensed treatment operator is not required at CWPF at all times.

  Councilmember Savidan moved to approve staff's recommendations as presented.
  Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

9. RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF SENATE BILL 208 AND HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
  BILL 456

  Assistant City Manager Sugano informed City Council that the City adopted a resolution in
  support of a similar bill in 2012, which was sponsored by U.S. Representative Berman,
  however, the bill was not signed into law. According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, the
  major difference between the current set of bills (Senate Bill 208 and House Bill 456) and the
  previous bill sponsored by Representative Berman is that the current set of bills specifically
  exempt helicopter operations related to emergency, law enforcement, and military activities,
  which in turn should more effectively reduce helicopter noise.

  George Kivett, Lomita resident, supported staff's recommendation and the resolution, and
  further added that both commercial and private flights should be flown over major
  commercial corridors instead of residential areas.

  John Bailey, President of the Southwest Torrance Homeowners’ Association and Member of
  the Los Angeles Area Helicopter Noise Coalition, congratulated Council on being proactive
  and for being the first city in Los Angeles County to support the bills regarding helicopter
  noise. Mr. Bailey added that the main purpose of the Los Angeles Residential Helicopter
  Noise Relief Act of 2013, is to make sure helicopter noise is reduced in order to provide
  residents with the quality of life they deserve, while at the same time not hurt helicopter
  manufacturers.

  Councilmember Savidan moved to adopt the resolution and authorize the Mayor to sign the
  letter of support. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion. Councilmember Gazeley
  noted that this resolution was in no way against the Torrance Airport, but rather focuses on
  finding a solution to an existing problem. Mayor Estrada also commented that she had
  received multiple complaints from residents regarding aircraft noise. The motion carried
  unanimously.

 ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:35 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
